title: Partner integration economics and risk playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook helps field teams and partner managers structure technical integrations with SI/ISV partners, align pilot economics, and accelerate safe co-sell motions. It focuses on three outcomes: 1) predictable unit economics for partner pilots, 2) minimized security/regulatory risk for enterprise prospects, and 3) a repeatable handoff from pilot to production across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment modes.

Audience
--------
- Sales engineers and partner solution architects
- Partner managers and channel account execs
- Deal engineering and pricing analysts
- Customer security reviewers (for the FAQ sections)

Top-line messaging (elevator and technical variants)
------------------------------------------------
- Elevator (executive): "Redwood lets your product teams add enterprise-grade LLM features with predictable latency and per-call economics — and a clear path to scale from pilot to production."
- Technical (platform/CTO): "We provide unified serving across hosted, reserved, and private footprints with transparent per-token cost controls, automatic fallbacks, and KMS/HSM integrations — so you don’t trade reliability for performance."

Competitive positioning highlights
--------------------------------
- Strength vs. cloud-managed endpoints: lower unit cost via automatic batching and prefix/KV caching; fine-grained routing by cost/latency; curated quantization profiles.
- Strength vs. self-hosted runtimes: opinionated rollout controls, SLA-backed dedicated capacity, and a developer console with token-level cost visibility.
- Weakness to acknowledge: for extremely latency-sensitive single-digit-ms workloads at hyperscale, custom kernel work can still beat hosted averages — call out profiling to set expectations.

Partner integration archetypes and recommended approach
-----------------------------------------------------
1) Embedded SDK integration (ISV feature add-on)
   - Use case: partner embeds Redwood SDK to add a summarization or search assistant feature inside their app.
   - Recommended deployment: Hosted API for quick pilot; Dedicated for predictable SLAs after commit.
   - Pilot length: 30–60 days.

2) Service-to-service API integration (SaaS platform)
   - Use case: partner routes anonymized requests from their service to Redwood with per-tenant rate limits.
   - Recommended deployment: Dedicated or Private (VPC) depending on data-sensitivity.
   - Pilot length: 60–90 days including compliance review.

3) On-prem / air-gapped integration (regulated customers)
   - Use case: customer requires on-prem inference with customer-managed KMS/HSM.
   - Recommended deployment: Redwood Private (on-prem package).
   - Pilot length: 90–180 days (packaging, network & security, validation).

Pilot economics framework (step-by-step)
---------------------------------------
1) Baseline measurement (Week 0)
   - Agree success metrics: queries/day, average input tokens, average response tokens, 95th-pct latency SLO.
   - Run a 3-day synthetic traffic run to establish p50/p95 token rates.

2) Technical profiling and choices (Week 1–2)
   - Profile model variants: accuracy vs. token cost tradeoffs (e.g., base-7B quantized vs. 13B fp16).
   - Enable prefix caching and KV cache for conversational flows; note expected hit rates.

3) Economics model (sample)
   - Inputs (example): queries/day=25k, avg in=120 tokens, avg out=220 tokens, pilot duration=60 days.
   - Select model: redwood-x-13b-quant (estimated token cost = $0.00008 per token).
   - Estimated cost = 25,000 * (120+220) * 60 * $0.00008 = $72,000 (gross token cost).

4) Cost reduction levers to propose during pilot
   - Caching: expected 15–40% token reduction for assistant-style workflows.
   - Quantization profile: switch to int8/4-bit variant for non-critical quality paths (saves 30–60%).
   - Batching and concurrency tuning: reduces latency tail and improves throughput efficiency.

Pricing scenario templates for partner pilots
-------------------------------------------
- Trial credit model (recommended for ISVs): Redwood issues a usage credit covering token spend up to $10k + 90 days of free basic observability. Partner bills implementation separately.
- Shared-risk pilot: partner pays a 50/50 split on gross token spend above the first $20k, with a cap at $75k.
- Consumption-to-commit conversion: 3x on average monthly pilot spend is the baseline for a 12-month reserved capacity commit.

Sample pricing JSON (reference for deal engineers)
--------------------------------------------------
{"pilot_name":"OEM-summarizer-trial","duration_days":"60","estimated_tokens":"(input+output)*queries*days","model_variant":"redwood-x-13b-quant","gross_token_cost_usd":"72000","redwood_trial_credit_usd":"10000"}

Operational checklist for SAs (pre-pilot to handoff)
----------------------------------------------------
1) Security questionnaire completed and annotated (owner: partner SA).
2) Identify data residency and encryption needs (KMS/HSM, log retention).
3) Agree test dataset and acceptance criteria (metrics + human eval pass/fail rules).
4) Configure cost-alerting thresholds in Redwood Console and partner dashboards.
5) Define rollback and fallback policies (model variant fallback + regional fallback).
6) Document runbook for outages and degradation (contact list + escalation matrix).

Sales playbook: motion templates and discovery questions
------------------------------------------------------
- Discovery: "What are your token volume expectations? Which flows are latency-sensitive vs. batch? Do you require customer-managed keys or VPC access?"
- Pilot close play: "If pilot meets X% of acceptance metrics and expected MRR uplift > $Y, propose Dedicated reserve at 3x monthly pilot spend."
- Upsell trigger cues: stable p95 latency, cache hit rate > 20%, successful security attestation

Common objections and rebuttals (field-friendly)
------------------------------------------------
- "We can self-host cheaper." -> "For initial go-to-market, self-hosting requires engineering time, ops headcount, and ongoing kernel/quantization tuning. Redwood provides measurable unit economics and an ops-free path to production with predictable SLAs; we can show a 6–12 week time-to-value delta."
- "We have compliance concerns about logs." -> "We support per-tenant log retention policies, redaction at ingestion, and optional private deployments with customer-managed KMS/HSM."

Security FAQ for partner prospects (concise answers)
--------------------------------------------------
Q: How is data encrypted in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.3 for transport; AES-256 for rest. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, or HSM appliances).

Q: Do you persist prompts or outputs?
A: By default, we store telemetry and usage for debugging and analytics. Customers can opt into no-persistence mode for prompts/outputs, and choose short retention windows or disable storage for sensitive flows.

Q: How are model updates handled to avoid regressions?
A: Redwood supports pinned model versions, staged canary rollouts, and automated quality gates tied to customer prompt sets. We recommend canaries against an acceptance prompt suite before any production switch.

Q: What logging/audit capabilities exist for compliance reviewers?
A: Token-level usage logs, API key events, provisioning changes, and admin audit trails are available via the Console and exported to S3/secure SIEM integrations.

Risk matrix and mitigation summary
--------------------------------
| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Owner |
|------|------------|--------|------------|-------|
| Data residency mismatch | Medium | High | Private or VPC deployment; contract SLAs | Partner SA |
| Unexpected token cost overrun | Medium | Medium | Cost alerts, trial credits, burst caps, model controls | Deal engineer |
| Latency SLO miss | Low | High | Dedicated capacity, autoscaling policy, regional routing | Infra eng |
| Quality regression on model update | Low | Medium | Pinned versions + regression evals | Applied ML |

Appendix: sample pitch deck outline (6 slides)
---------------------------------------------
1) Opportunity & pain (customer metrics)
2) Redwood technical approach + deployment options
3) Pilot plan & success metrics (30/60/90 day milestones)
4) Economics: sample pilot cost and reduction levers
5) Security/compliance summary & references
6) Next steps & commitment ask (options: trial credit, shared-risk pilot, commit)
